This is sand leveling, or topdressing. It creates a more level surface for your lawn by filling in low areas. I use masonry sand since I have Bermuda grass. If you have a cool season grass type, a screened topsoil may be better. I like to put a little fertilizer down prior to, and after to ensure bermuda is growing aggressively through the sand. 21 hours in 90 seconds👨🏽‍🌾 ⚠️Flash Warning⚠️ This house was bought near the end of 2025 and the garden was a right state!  I was called in to replace the fence panels and totally rip out the garden  (not the posts, they are a bit crooked but they are still standing😅)  I started with the fence panels, then began to totally clear the area of weeds and any other debris in the garden.  We added 2 railway sleepers at the back for a little flower bed. Then a thick layer of top soil was spread and we rolled out the turf. Then we moved 4 tonnes of hardcore to the back through the house!  Backbreaking stuff.  Thanks to my pal @Wagwarn Abel for jumping on and giving me a hand 🙏 This is obviously unfinished but I think the owner was going to slab the rest himself, so our job is done here for now! As always I wanna know what would YOU do now? There's a bed at the back that's totally empty!  I read and appreciate any comments and genuinely like reading your suggestions🙏 Thanks so much for watching anyway, follow if you haven't already for more vids like this!! Love, Tom Butler  #satisfying #timelapse #landscaping #gardening

Even in late summer, mulch can play an important role in keeping your landscape healthy. A fresh layer of mulch helps retain soil moisture during hot, dry periods, reducing stress on plants and helping roots stay cooler. It also suppresses weeds that compete with plants for water and nutrients, while gradually adding organic matter to the soil as it breaks down. Mulch can also protect soil from heavy summer rain and erosion, keeping your beds looking clean and well-maintained. Late summer is a great time to refresh mulch before the cooler fall weather arrives. #greenwich #connecticut #landscaping #landscapedesign #cleanup
